title: India Rolls Out Sweeping Tax and Digital Payments Overhaul Across 2026
excerpt: The new Income Tax Act, GST 2.0, and RBI stricter authentication rules are collectively reshaping how India taxes, transacts, and regulates its booming digital economy.
body:
• India's new Income Tax Act, 2025, effective since April 1, 2026, replaces the six-decade-old 1961 Act with simplified provisions, reducing rules from 399 to 190 and forms from 511 to 333
  • GST 2.0 reforms consolidated indirect tax rates into two main slabs of 5% and 18%, abolishing the 12% and 28% tiers for most goods, while new e-invoice and e-way bill requirements took effect August 1
  • RBI's new digital payment authentication framework mandates two-factor verification for all UPI, card, and wallet transactions, while the Digital Rupee gains official recognition as a payment mode
  • The National Payments Corporation of India extended the deadline for implementing a 30% cap on any single UPI app's transaction share to December 31, 2026, offering relief to PhonePe and Google Pay

India's tax and digital payments landscape is undergoing its most significant transformation in decades, with a series of interconnected reforms reshaping how 350 million taxpayers file returns and over a billion digital payment users transact daily.

The centerpiece is the Income Tax Act, 2025, which took effect on April 1, 2026, replacing the sprawling Income Tax Act of 1961. The new legislation condenses 819 sections into 536, reorganizes compliance structures, and introduces a unified "Tax Year" concept, eliminating the confusing distinction between "Assessment Year" and "Previous Year" that had long frustrated taxpayers and professionals alike.

A Leaner Tax Code

"The formalising of the new income tax framework is undoubtedly one of the most significant developments this year," said Richa Sawhney, Partner at Grant Thornton Bharat. "Focus on simplification, ease of compliance and thrust on use of technology will have a far-reaching impact in shaping a modern and future-ready taxation regime."

The accompanying Income Tax Rules, 2026, notified by the Central Board of Direct Taxes in March, cut the number of rules from 399 to 190 and forms from 511 to 333. Pre-filled returns, automated validation, and AI-enabled filing assistance are now embedded in the digital compliance infrastructure.

"A Leaner Tax Code "The formalising of the new income tax framework is undoubtedly one of the most significant developments this year," said Richa Sawhney, Partner at Grant Thornton Bharat."

Transfer pricing norms have been rationalized by merging IT, ITeS, KPO, and R&D services into a single category with a 15.5% safe harbour margin. The eligibility threshold has been raised to 2,000 crore rupees from 300 crore, with five-year validity and automated approvals.

GST 2.0 and Customs Modernization

On the indirect tax front, GST 2.0 reforms introduced in September 2025 simplified the rate structure to two main slabs — 5% and 18% — with 40% reserved for sin and luxury goods. The move abolished the 12% and 28% tiers for most items, correcting rate inversions in labour-intensive sectors and lowering costs for consumer goods, vehicles, healthcare, and agricultural inputs.

New e-invoice and e-way bill system changes that took effect August 1, 2026, mandate a "Ship-to GSTIN" field for certain transactions and introduce an optional e-way bill closure facility after goods delivery. Customs reforms now include defined timelines for provisional assessments and allow voluntary revisions after clearance without penalty.

Digital Payments Get Stricter Security

The Reserve Bank of India's Authentication Mechanisms for Digital Payment Transactions Directions, 2025, now require mandatory two-factor authentication for all digital payments — UPI, debit and credit cards, mobile wallets, and internet banking. At least one authentication factor must be dynamic, such as a one-time password or biometric verification.

The framework also introduces risk-based authentication, where low-risk transactions may proceed with lighter verification while high-value or unusual payments trigger additional checks. The Digital Rupee, India's central bank digital currency, has been officially recognized as an electronic payment method under the new tax rules.

Meanwhile, the National Payments Corporation of India extended its deadline for implementing a 30% cap on any single UPI app's market share to December 31, 2026. The delay provides temporary relief to Walmart-backed PhonePe and Google Pay, which together handle over 85% of transactions on the network that processes more than 13 billion transactions monthly.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For non-resident Indians, Budget 2026 introduced targeted reforms to ease property transactions. Resident buyers purchasing property from NRI sellers no longer need to obtain a separate Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number — TDS can be deposited using a PAN-based challan instead, effective October 2026. A six-month Foreign Assets Disclosure Scheme offers NRIs and small taxpayers a window to regularize past lapses with limited penalties.

The expanded digital access powers granted to tax authorities — covering email servers, social media accounts, online investment accounts, and cloud servers during investigations — have raised privacy concerns among legal experts, particularly for NRIs managing cross-border financial affairs.

What's Next

The government has extended tax exemptions for foreign companies providing equipment to contract manufacturers in India until March 2041, a significant win for Apple and other tech giants expanding production in the country. India is set to manufacture 26% of the world's iPhones in 2026, up from 6% four years ago.

With the first filing season under the new Income Tax Act approaching — returns for Tax Year 2026-27 will be due in 2027 — the true test of these reforms will be whether simplification on paper translates to reduced compliance friction in practice.
